examples.text: Подождите, как это за два года?
examples.trans: Wait, what do you mean over two years?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'day', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Она из далёкого Владивостока на два дня прилетела!
examples.trans: She flew in from distant Vladivostok for two days!

examples.text: Ты ласково улыбался мне целый день!
examples.trans: You smiled tenderly at me the whole day!

examples.text: Добрый день, вас беспокоит лейтенант полиции Судник.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Police Lieutenant Sudnik speaking.

прилететь.gloss: to arrive (by air), to fly in

meanings.en: to arrive (by air), to fly in
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'лететь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to arrive', forming an aspectual pair with 'прилетать'.

examples.text: Она из далёкого Владивостока на два дня прилетела!
examples.trans: She flew in from distant Vladivostok for two days!

examples.text: Мы прилетели на сделку.
examples.trans: We flew in for the deal.

examples.text: Когда ты прилетишь?
examples.trans: When will you fly in?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'Ivanovna', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Вера Ивановна, извините, мы ужасно спешим!
examples.trans: Vera Ivanovna, excuse us, we are in a terrible hurry!

examples.text: Вера Ивановна, сейчас я вам всё объясню.
examples.trans: Vera Ivanovna, I will explain everything to you right now.

examples.text: Вера Ивановна, а где у вас бокалы?
examples.trans: Vera Ivanovna, where do you keep your wineglasses?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('we') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Вчера вечером у нас случилась большая оплошность.
examples.trans: Last night a big indiscretion happened between us.

examples.text: Вера Ивановна, извините, мы ужасно спешим!
examples.trans: Vera Ivanovna, excuse us, we are in a terrible hurry!

examples.text: Лёва, давай быстрее, нам пора на кухню!
examples.trans: Lyova, hurry up, it is time for us to go to the kitchen!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'terribly'.

examples.text: Вера Ивановна, извините, мы ужасно спешим!
examples.trans: Vera Ivanovna, excuse us, we are in a terrible hurry!

examples.text: Ужасно! Очень плохой костюм!
examples.trans: Terrible! A very bad suit!

examples.text: На улице сегодня ужасно холодно.
examples.trans: It is terribly cold outside today.

спешить.gloss: to hurry, be in a rush

meanings.en: to hurry, be in a rush
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'пешить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to hurry', forming an aspectual pair with 'поспешить'.

examples.text: Вера Ивановна, извините, мы ужасно спешим!
examples.trans: Vera Ivanovna, excuse us, we are in a terrible hurry!

examples.text: Я сейчас очень спешу обратно на кухню!
examples.trans: I am in a big hurry to get back to the kitchen right now!

examples.text: Что случилось? Куда ты спешишь?
examples.trans: What happened? Where are you rushing to?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('let's') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Давай убирать!
examples.trans: Let's clean up!

examples.text: Давай, пока!
examples.trans: See you, bye!

examples.text: Аркаша, давай убирать!
examples.trans: Arkasha, let's clean up!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'fast', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Наша Ева вообще очень быстрая и умелая.
examples.trans: Our Eva is very quick and skillful in general.

examples.text: Нам нужен быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: We need fast internet.

examples.text: Они сказали, что устанавливают быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: They said that they were installing fast internet.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'it's time'.

examples.text: Лёва, давай быстрее, нам пора на кухню!
examples.trans: Lyova, hurry up, it is time for us to go to the kitchen!

examples.text: Пора домой.
examples.trans: Time to go home.

examples.text: Нам пора.
examples.trans: It's time for us to go.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: А у меня на кухне строгий начальник!
examples.trans: And I have a strict boss in the kitchen!

examples.text: Лёва, давай быстрее, нам пора на кухню!
examples.trans: Lyova, hurry up, it is time for us to go to the kitchen!

examples.text: Я сейчас очень спешу обратно на кухню!
examples.trans: I am in a big hurry to get back to the kitchen right now!
